Save this before you land at Narita with an Asakusa hotel booked: four quick checks that can save you a 670 m walk with your bags on arrival day, and again on the way back 👇

📋 THE CHECKLIST

1️⃣ Read the line name in your hotel's access notes. "Asakusa Station" can mean the Toei Asakusa Line, the Ginza Line, Tobu or the Tsukuba Express.

2️⃣ From Narita, ride the Access Express. It runs through to the Toei Asakusa Line: 70 minutes and ¥1,380 on our sample, with no change.

3️⃣ Use exit A2b if you need step-free access. A hotel next to SORA Kaminarimon is about 250 m away; one by the Tsukuba Express station is about 670 m.

4️⃣ Plan the way back too. On our sample departure the Access Express left Asakusa at 09:21 and reached Terminal 1 at 10:32, again from the Toei station.

💡 WHEN THE TSUKUBA EXPRESS SIDE MAKES SENSE

🎮 Akihabara mornings: 5 minutes and ¥230 from the TX station.

🎒 Light luggage, so the walk on arrival and departure day doesn't matter.

💴 A clearly lower price on your own dates, checked for the same nights and the same number of guests. On ours, 14–17 Dec 2026, the TX-side hotel we checked cost ¥655 more than one by the Toei station.

🏮 Get it right and your first Asakusa evening starts with a short walk to the lanterns, not a long one with a suitcase.
